text.insert: A Mac capture runs from one press of the Record shortcut to a finished bundle. While it records, Annotator takes the screen video, the microphone, clicks, scrolls, keys, the draw-modifier ink and pins, and a log of the windows on screen. This page covers how a recording starts, what it records, how ink and pins work, how pause and resume cut time out, and how displays are handled. The files a capture leaves and the paste are on

props.title: Conditions for a kept press

text.insert: Every left press on the Mac passes the tap, so the cheap checks come first. Until the setting, the recording and the modifiers say a press can be a draw-press, the tap only reads two system press counters. When in doubt a press passes, because a missed pin costs a click and a press kept by mistake costs the app its click.
would, its drags are kept, and its release ends it as
would. A pause or a finish during a kept press drops the press but keeps the rest of it from the app until the button comes up. Five rules keep that judgment right.
The tap reads the window list for each press it judges and reuses no answer. The read costs the tap thread a median 0.4 ms, and 48.6 ms at most over 21 windows.
A press on one of Annotator's own windows, such as the capsule, goes to it. A press on a macOS prompt (
In a Window or iPhone capture a press passes unless it goes to that window (
): the window by its id, or the iPhone mirror by its process.
When another window is in front, the tap asks the window server which window takes the press (
), and no answer passes. A minimized window or one on another Space keeps nothing.
The mouse monitor keeps its own answer for 250 ms at one point (
) to decide what is recorded, and the tap never reads it. A press the tap lets through drops no pin.
"Left over from a chord" is one latch (
) that ink, pins and kept presses all read. So ⌘⇧ with ⌘ let go neither draws, drops a pin nor is kept.
The tap counts each modifier change in key order (
). The poller marks the latch first (
) and counts its sample only if the tap saw no change since (
While the tap is on, a poller sample can set the latch but never clear it. Only the tap's own event that the draw modifier is up clears it.
A change the tap never sees, such as under Secure Input, leaves the latch on until the tap sees the draw modifier let go. Without a tap every poller sample counts.
One party starts and ends a draw-press: the key tap, or the mouse monitor with the polled buttons.

text.insert: The movie, the audio and the candidates each follow more rules when they are cut.

A 2-minute, 172 MB movie with two pauses takes 0.11 s. A cut between keyframes is trimmed by the edit list, which AVFoundation and ffmpeg both follow (
The pauses move onto the movie's own clock first (
A Mac movie that cannot be cut is deleted rather than kept with its pauses, and the keyframes then come from the candidates. An iPhone capture fails instead.
The microphone opens some hundred ms after the capture clock starts, so the audio carries its own start (
), and the pauses move onto that clock first.
The offset is the first buffer's arrival less how long before that CPAL's timestamp says its first sample was captured. It counts the device's latency as well as the buffer.
Every engine times words from the WAV's first sample, so
later, in one place for Apple, Deepgram, Hex and a command.
A live transcription that heard the pauses is dropped, and the cut WAV is transcribed instead.
No candidate is kept during a pause (
), so a long pause does not thin the rest.
When every candidate falls in a pause,
puts in one blank frame, never a paused image, because a bundle needs a frame.

The other design stops each recorder while paused and keeps a running offset. That needs a pause in four recorders that start and stop at their own pace. ScreenCaptureKit's recording output cannot pause, so the movie would be written in segments and joined. Each recorder would lose a slightly different span, which is how audio and video drift apart.

One list of spans on one clock, applied once, cannot drift, and the live path stays as it is. The cost is that the pause stays on disk until finish, the microphone indicator stays on, and the movie is rewritten once when a pause happened.
